value.rationale: The Shrikhande and rook graphs are the canonical nonisomorphic strongly regular 16-vertex graphs with the same (16,6,2,2) parameters. Their equal minimum contagious-set size hides quantitatively different complete optimum families (720 and 864), geometric orbit partitions (six versus two) and token-jumping radii/diameters (4,5 versus 4,4). This natural cospectral comparison distinguishes dynamic optimization and mobility properties not fixed by intersection parameters, rather than recomputing only a known seed number. Complete finite exactness has independent mathematical relevance; no unrestricted generalization is claimed.
